findings.title: Device limit is bypassed because the device ID is cached before the store write
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. With the new limit enforcement, a new device over the limit gets ErrDeviceLimitReached from the store, but the cache entry stays. The next request from that device hits localCache.Get and returns nil without calling the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds and the device is never counted. Parallel requests from the same device can also pass immediately while the first request is still being rejected. Move SetDefault until after a successful create/update, or delete the key on error.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices in one DB session, then performs the upsert in another session. Two concurrent requests from different new device IDs can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. Because device IDs are supplied by the client and requests can be parallel, this is reachable. Enforce the limit in a transaction with an appropriate lock/serialization, or use an atomic insert-and-check mechanism.

findings.title: RowsAffected()==0 is treated as a limit hit, but MySQL reports changed rows, not matched rows
findings.body: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever RowsAffected() is zero. On MySQL (unless clientFoundRows=true is configured), UPDATE returns the number of rows actually changed, not matched. If an existing device at the limit sends a request with the same client_ip/user_agent and the same second-precision updated_at as the stored row, the UPDATE is a no-op, RowsAffected() is 0, and a legitimate existing device is rejected. This can happen when multiple Grafana instances handle the same device in the same second because the in-process cache does not coordinate replicas. Check existence separately or use a driver-independent matched-row approach.

findings.title: Device-limit tests only cover the store's rejection path
findings.body: The new test only calls ProvideAnonDBStore directly and checks that a second new device ID returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. It does not cover (a) an existing device still updating when the limit is reached, (b) the Anonymous auth client rejecting an over-limit device, or (c) the local-cache interaction that currently allows the device after the first rejection. Add a service/auth-level integration test with a nonzero AnonymousDeviceLimit.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is not documented or added to defaults.ini
findings.body: The PR adds a user-facing auth.anonymous device_limit option, but no sample/default config or documentation is updated. Users cannot discover the new setting from defaults.ini or the configuration reference. Add it to conf/defaults.ini and the anonymous auth configuration docs.
